title: Can a tribunal compound interest the contract never mentions?

scenes.dialogue: Advocates, if a contract says nothing about interest, can an arbitral tribunal still award interest that is compounded every year?
The State never issued a completion certificate, and the tribunal added fourteen percent interest, compounded yearly. Two objections. Which one survives?
scenes.shown: The State never issued a completion certificate, and the tribunal added 14% interest, compounded yearly. Two objections. Which one survives?

scenes.dialogue: Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. An Allahabad High Court bench of Honourable Chief Justice Arun Bhansali and Honourable Justice Jaspreet Singh ruled.
The Public Works Department hired a contractor to widen and strengthen the Raya Math Road in Mathura district. The work was completed in August two thousand nine.
scenes.shown: The Public Works Department hired a contractor to widen and strengthen the Raya-Math Road in Mathura district. The work was completed in August 2009.

scenes.dialogue: The contractor claimed nearly twenty four crore rupees. The tribunal rejected its final bill, but awarded about one crore fifty seven lakh, plus costs.
scenes.shown: The contractor claimed nearly ₹24 crore. The tribunal rejected its final bill, but awarded about ₹1.57 crore, plus costs.

scenes.dialogue: The Commercial Court at Lucknow upheld the award. In appeal, the State argued that no completion certificate was ever issued, so the work was never complete.
On interest, the State said the contract is silent, and the Interest Act bars interest upon interest. The contractor replied: banks compound every quarter.

scenes.dialogue: Finally, what did the High Court decide? With the work proved, a missing certificate did not mean it was incomplete. The State never gave notice of any defect.
The Court held that yearly compounding is interest upon interest, which needs a contract clause. So the award was modified to fourteen percent simple, in two stages.
scenes.shown: The Court held that yearly compounding is interest upon interest, which needs a contract clause. So the award was modified to 14% simple, in two stages.
